evidence.support_text: The percentage of B220+ cells increased by 72% in the 75% CIN treatment group compared with vehicle control mice.

evidence.assay_type: Immunofluorescent staining of lymph node subpopulations
evidence.experimental_conditions: Mice were treated on ears with 25 µL of 75% CIN on both sides of each ear for 4 consecutive days; lymph nodes collected and cells labeled for CD4.
evidence.support_text: A 26% decrease in the percentage of CD4+ T cells was observed in the 75% CIN treatment group compared with vehicle control mice.

evidence.assay_type: Immunofluorescent staining of lymph node subpopulations
evidence.experimental_conditions: Mice were treated on ears with 25 µL of 75% CIN on both sides of each ear for 4 consecutive days; lymph nodes collected and cells labeled for immunoglobulin.
evidence.support_text: The percentage of Ig+ cells increased by 52% in the 75% CIN treatment group compared with vehicle control mice.

evidence.assay_type: In vitro restimulation of draining lymph node cells with haptenated APCs after in vivo sensitization
evidence.experimental_conditions: C57BL/6 mice, sensitized for 5 days with TNCB; in vitro restimulation of draining lymph node cells with haptenated antigen-presenting cells.
evidence.support_text: In C57BL/6 mice sensitized for 5 days with the hapten TNCB, upon in vitro restimulation of draining lymph node cells with haptenated antigen-presenting cells, an unusually high frequency of about 50–100 CD8+ T-cell precursors per 10^5 LN cells was detected.

evidence.assay_type: in vitro restimulation with anti-CD3 + IL-4 capture flow cytometry
evidence.experimental_conditions: Treatment: 0.5% oxalozone on dorsum of both ears for 3 consecutive days; mice sacrificed 24h after last application; ear-draining LNC prepared; B220+ cells depleted; restimulation for 5h with plate-bound anti-CD3 at 37°C; IL-4 captured and detected with PE-labelled anti-IL-4 antibody; detection by flow cytometry and MACS enrichment.
evidence.support_text: Mice were treated daily on 3 consecutive days with 0.5% oxalozone (OXA) on the dorsum of both ears. Twenty-four hours after the last application, ear-draining lymph node cells were prepared, depleted of B220+ cells, and restimulated for 5 h with plate-bound anti-CD3 antibody at 37°C. IL-4 captured on the cell surface was detected with a PE-labelled anti-IL-4 antibody, and dot blots showed LNCs double stained for IL-4 and CD4 before and after enrichment, indicating IL-4 release from CD4+ T cells in response to oxalozone treatment.

evidence.assay_type: in vivo draining lymph node cell enumeration
evidence.experimental_conditions: murine model, dermal exposure, 3 days
evidence.support_text: Biologically significant increases in B220+ and IgE + B220+ cells in the DLNs were observed only for 3,4-hexanedione and 2,3-heptanedione.

evidence.assay_type: in vivo sensitization test (one induction and three challenges, 1 week apart)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse, one induction and three challenges 1 week apart, BrdU-labeling, measurement 24 h after final treatment, vehicle control.
evidence.support_text: It also significantly increased the ... BrdU-labeled lymphocytes in lymph nodes by ... 173%, respectively, compared with the vehicle control (Fig. 6c).

evidence.assay_type: in vivo sensitization test (one induction and three challenges, 1 week apart)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse, one induction and three challenges 1 week apart, BrdU-labeling, measurement 24 h after final treatment, vehicle control.
evidence.support_text: Results also showed that DNFB treatments significantly increased ... BrdU-labeled lymphocytes in lymph nodes by ... 69.5%, respectively, compared with the vehicle control (Fig. 4c).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Intermediate (0.3%) or high (0.5%) dose DNFB painted on ear of C57BL/6 or BALB/C mice; draining lymph nodes analyzed at day 5 post-treatment.
evidence.support_text: Intermediate dose- and high dose-induced ICD reactions increased during the days following DNFB painting and evolved in an ACD reaction from day 5 with priming/expansion of DNFB-specific CD8+ T cells in draining lymph nodes of C57BL/6 or BALB/C mice.

evidence.assay_type: in vivo thiol depletion (MBB flow cytometry)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse, intraperitoneal injection, 4.5 mmol/kg DEM, 1 hour, lymph node cells analyzed by MBB fluorescence
evidence.support_text: An intraperitoneal dose of 4.5 mmol/kg diethyl maleate (DEM) led to a 73% decrease in the thiol content of lymph node cells, as measured by MBB fluorescence, in mice 1 hour after injection.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse lymph node cells collected on day 13 after DNCB exposure; stimulated with PMA/ionomycin for 5 h for intracellular staining.
evidence.support_text: DNCB treatment induced an increase in the percentages of IL-2-producing lymphocytes in both T cell subsets, with significant results in the CD8+ cells (46.5 ± 0.7% of CD4+ and 20.9 ± 1.3% of CD8+ cell populations) compared to AOO (44.3 ± 0.6% CD4+ and 14.0 ± 0.9% CD8+).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse lymph node cells collected on day 13 after TMA exposure; stimulated with PMA/ionomycin for 5 h for intracellular staining.
evidence.support_text: A significant reduction in the percentages of IL-2-producing CD8+ cells (9.0 ± 0.9%) was observed following TMA exposure, compared to AOO (14.0 ± 0.9%).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse lymph node cells collected on day 13 after TMA exposure; stimulated with PMA/ionomycin for 5 h for intracellular staining.
evidence.support_text: Compared to AOO vehicle, TMA induced a clearly significant increase in the proportion of CD8+ cells capable of producing IFN-γ on day 13, from 17.9 ± 3.4% (AOO) to 38.7 ± 1.4% (TMA).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse lymph node cells collected on day 13 after TMA exposure; stimulated with PMA/ionomycin for 5 h for intracellular staining.
evidence.support_text: On day 13, a significant reduction in the percentages of IL-2-producing CD4+ lymphocytes was observed following TMA exposure (34.8 ± 1.8%) compared to AOO vehicle (44.3 ± 0.6%).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse lymph node cells collected on day 13 after TMA exposure; stimulated with PMA/ionomycin for 5 h for intracellular staining.
evidence.support_text: The presence of CD4+ lymphocytes positive for IL-4 was clearly observed in the lymph node cells isolated from TMA-sensitized mice, representing 1.0 ± 0.3% of the CD4+ population on day 13, while no IL-4 positive cells were found in AOO-exposed mice.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse lymph node cells collected on day 13 after TMA exposure; stimulated with PMA/ionomycin for 5 h for intracellular staining.
evidence.support_text: Very few CD4+ lymphocytes were found positive for IFN-γ on day 13 following AOO, TMA, and DNCB exposure, with no significant difference between the TMA- and DNCB-exposed mice.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse lymph node cells collected on day 18 after TMA exposure; stimulated with PMA/ionomycin for 5 h for intracellular staining.
evidence.support_text: On day 18, the percentage of CD4+ cells positive for IL-4 in TMA-sensitized mice was 1.6 ± 0.3% of the CD4+ population.

evidence.assay_type: intracellular cytokine staining by flow cytometry
evidence.experimental_conditions: 12.5% CIN (v/v) treatment group; 25 µL per ear for 4 consecutive days; ALN harvested one day after final treatment; mouse (strain not specified).
evidence.support_text: A significant increase in the percentage of CD8⁺ IFN-γ cells was also observed in the 12.5% CIN treatment group but not at other doses.

evidence.assay_type: human repeated insult patch test (modified Draize-Shelanski RIPT)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Product: moisturizer containing 0.3% Quaternium-15; modified Draize-Shelanski RIPT; challenge patches applied to induction and untreated sites; 205 healthy subjects
evidence.support_text: A moisturizer containing 0.3% Quaternium-15 was evaluated in a modified Draize-Shelanski RIPT using 205 healthy subjects. Ten subjects reacted with erythema at challenge, but none of these reactions were considered significant or indicative of irritation or sensitization by the authors.

evidence.assay_type: human repeated insult patch test (triple freeze, repeated induction)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Re-induction of previous non-reactors with same triple freeze procedure; challenge with 5% NiCl₂ non-occluded; subjects: 19 non-reactors from first induction
evidence.support_text: Some non-reactors from the first triple freeze induction were re-exposed using the same procedure; 26% (5/19) of this group were sensitized, showing that the sensitization rate can be raised by prolonged exposure.

evidence.assay_type: human repeated insult patch test and human maximization test
evidence.experimental_conditions: human repeated insult patch test and human maximization test; no further details provided
evidence.support_text: Additionally, no reactions indicative of skin sensitization were observed in both the human repeated insult patch test and the human maximization test to benzyl acetate (RIFM, 1987; RIFM, 1988a; RIFM, 1988b; NTP, 1993; RIFM, 1988c; RIFM, 1988d; RIFM, 1961; RIFM, 1975a; RIFM, 1975b; RIFM, 1975c; RIFM, 1975d; RIFM, 1975e).

evidence.assay_type: Human repeated insult patch test with SLS pretreatment
evidence.experimental_conditions: 22 human subjects; pretreatment with 5% sodium lauryl sulfate for 24 hours; occlusive application of formulation at 48-hour intervals; challenge 10-14 days after last application
evidence.support_text: No evidence of contact sensitization was observed when 22 subjects were treated with 5% sodium lauryl sulfate 24 hours prior to treatment with the formulation (6% Beeswax and 6% Synthetic Beeswax) under occlusive conditions at 48-hour intervals, with challenge 10-14 days after the last application.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.8% t-BGE in perchloroethylene, repeated insult patch test
evidence.support_text: Two of fifty-six subjects showed dermal sensitization to t-BGE on repeated-insult patch testing with 0.8% t-BGE in perchloroethylene (Vaughn and Keeler, 1976).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 3% in 70:30 ethyl alcohol/deionized water solution, occluded patch, 227 male and female subjects aged 16-79, 0.2 ml test material dried for 30 min on absorbent pad, induction patches for 24 h on Mondays/Wednesdays/Fridays for 3 weeks, challenge patch applied 2 weeks after final induction, scoring at 24 and 72 h
evidence.support_text: Only one person had a positive (score = 1) reaction after the first induction patch was removed. A score of 1 was described as mild erythema covering most of the test site. This was the only positive score for this person and was the only positive score for both the induction and challenge phases for all volunteers. The authors stated that Phytantriol did not indicate a potential for dermal irritation or allergic contact sensitization (Consumer Product Testing Co. 2004a).

evidence.assay_type: modified Draize repeat insult patch test
evidence.experimental_conditions: 50% w/v in liquid paraffin; 91 healthy volunteers (18-65 years); induction: 9 applications over 18-19 days; challenge on day 35; scoring 1 and 49 hours post-challenge; negative control: liquid paraffin.
evidence.support_text: In a modified Draize repeat insult patch test on 91 healthy volunteers, Glyceryl Palmitate Lactate (50% w/v in liquid paraffin) did not induce skin irritation or sensitization (Danisco Ingredients 1996).

evidence.assay_type: modified Draize repeat insult patch test
evidence.experimental_conditions: Patches applied for one week; prolonged period of occlusion
evidence.support_text: In a modified Draize repeat insult patch test assay, the clonidine TTS demonstrated a potential for producing allergic contact dermatitis, which has been confirmed by clinical experience. The frequency of sensitization varies from 0% to 50%, and in one study 90% of a group of 72 sensitized patients presented with contact sensitivity by 20 weeks.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 50% w/v Glyceryl Palmitate Lactate in liquid paraffin; 74 subjects; Finn chambers; occlusive patches.
evidence.support_text: Glyceryl Palmitate Lactate (50% w/v in liquid paraffin) did not induce skin irritation or sensitization in 74 subjects patch tested (Finn chambers) in a modified Draize repeat-insult patch test.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Suntan cream containing 0.003% Propyl Gallate; occlusive patches on upper backs; Monday, Wednesday, Friday for 3 weeks; 2-week nontreatment period; two consecutive 48-h challenge patches scored at 48 and 96 h.
evidence.support_text: A modified Draize-Shelanski repeat-insult patch test on 150 subjects using a suntan cream containing 0.003% Propyl Gallate. Method as above. No reactions were observed. Investigators reported no instances of sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Suntan oil containing 0.003% Propyl Gallate; occlusive patches on upper backs; Monday, Wednesday, Friday for 3 weeks; 2-week nontreatment period; two consecutive 48-h challenge patches scored at 48 and 96 h.
evidence.support_text: A modified Draize-Shelanski repeat-insult patch test on 151 subjects using a suntan oil containing 0.003% Propyl Gallate. Occlusive patches applied to upper backs on M/W/F for 3 weeks; 2-week rest; two 48-h challenge patches. Eight scores of 1 and two scores of 2 were observed on induction, but no positive reactions on challenge. Investigators reported no instances of sensitization.

evidence.assay_type: Modified Human Repeated Insult Patch Test
evidence.experimental_conditions: 3% in Alcohol SD 39C, 3543 µg/cm², occlusion on back for 24h 3 days/week for 3 weeks, then 1 week rest, challenge with 4 daily applications, scores at 24 and 48h
evidence.support_text: In a modified Repeat Insult Patch Test with 52 subjects, 0.2 ml samples of 3% 2-methyl-4-phenylpentanol in Alcohol SD 39C induced adverse skin reactions in 7 subjects, but the investigator concluded that the responses were not immunological in nature, and that the test material did not produce responses of sufficient intensity or consistency to characterize it as sensitizing.

evidence.assay_type: modified human repeated insult patch test (HRIPT)
evidence.experimental_conditions: modified HRIPT, 10% octocrylene (w/w), applied to skin after ablative fractional resurfacing (resurfacing group, n=30)
evidence.support_text: In the modified HRIPT, octocrylene (10% w/w) showed a significantly higher sensitization rate in the resurfacing group (30 subjects who applied sunscreen after ablative fractional skin resurfacing) compared to the non-resurfacing group (30 subjects who applied sunscreen on intact skin).

evidence.assay_type: modified human repeated insult patch test (HRIPT)
evidence.experimental_conditions: modified HRIPT, broad-spectrum sunscreen containing Licochalcone-A (as is), applied to skin after ablative fractional resurfacing (resurfacing group, n=30)
evidence.support_text: The broad-spectrum sunscreen containing Licochalcone-A showed a significantly higher sensitization rate in the modified HRIPT in the resurfacing group (30 subjects who applied sunscreen after ablative fractional skin resurfacing) compared to the non-resurfacing group (30 subjects who applied sunscreen on intact skin).

evidence.assay_type: Modified Shelanski method (human repeated insult patch test)
evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.2% NNT emulsion; 52 female subjects; modified Shelanski method; 24 h occlusive patch applications; induction and challenge phases; 10 applications.
evidence.support_text: Human repeated insult patch test was conducted using a modified Shelanski method on 52 female subjects. For NNT 0.2% emulsion, the table shows 2 responders out of 52 with a response score of 1.0/2.0, a Mean Irritation Index of 0.02, and sensitization indicated as '–', meaning lack of sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Repeat insult patch test on 66 healthy female volunteers; concentrations of 1% and 5% in vehicle formulation
evidence.support_text: There were no adverse reactions noted during the course of the repeat insult patch test, demonstrating that the extract causes neither skin irritation nor sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 50% w/w Glyceryl Diboleate in liquid paraffin; 82 subjects; occlusive patch test.
evidence.support_text: Sensitization was not induced in any of 82 subjects patch tested with 50% w/w Glyceryl Diboleate (in liquid paraffin) in a repeat-insult, occlusive patch test. Mild erythema was observed in seven subjects during induction.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.1% sodium hypochlorite (Amu-Skin) evaluated neat; blinded, randomized, occlusive repeated insult patch study; 194 subjects.
evidence.support_text: A Repeated Insult Patch Study was performed by Amuchina evaluating 0.1% sodium hypochlorite (Amu-Skin) neat to determine its ability to sensitize the skin of normal volunteer subjects using a blinded, randomized, occlusive repeated insult patch study. With 194 subjects, there was no evidence of sensitization to Amu-Skin or to the vehicle.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.2% ACA in either DEP or 1:3 DEP:EtOH vehicle, applied to human subjects
evidence.support_text: AAG tested at 0.5% and ACA tested at 0.2% induced no irritation or sensitization in repeated insult patch tests, whether the vehicle was DEP or 1:3 DEP:EtOH (RIFM 1989a, 1989b).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.5% AAG in either DEP or 1:3 DEP:EtOH vehicle, applied to human subjects
evidence.support_text: AAG tested at 0.5% and ACA tested at 0.2% induced no irritation or sensitization in repeated insult patch tests, whether the vehicle was DEP or 1:3 DEP:EtOH (RIFM 1989a, 1989b).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.8% AAG in DEP vehicle, applied to human subjects
evidence.support_text: When AAG was tested in a repeated-insult patch test at 0.8%, no irritation or sensitization was observed when the vehicle was DEP (RIFM 1990a).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human subjects; repeated insult patch test (RIFM, 1973).
evidence.support_text: No reactions indicative of skin sensitization were observed for linalyl cinnamate in the repeated insult patch test.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction with 0.5% GA, challenge; 109 subjects
evidence.support_text: ...but with 0.5% induction there was a challenge reaction in one of 109 subjects.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 9 sequential 24-hour induction applications and 2 concurrently conducted 24-hour challenge applications (1 at induction site and 1 at naive site); application using partially occlusive patching device with 2 cm x 2 cm absorbent pad (150 µL product) on 2 cm x 4 cm plastic film; 111 healthy participants (64 males, 47 females; 18-74 years old); 109 completed induction phase; 101 completed challenge phase.
evidence.support_text: The skin irritation and sensitization potential of a body and hand cream containing 0.59% methyl glucose dioleate was evaluated in a repeated insult patch test (double-blind conditions) that initially involved 111 healthy participants. The product was neither a clinically significant skin irritant nor a sensitizer under the conditions of this study.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 8% concentration; 50 subjects
evidence.support_text: Peru balsam produced no evidence of skin sensitization when tested at 8% concentration on 50 subjects with a repeated insult method (Shelanski and Shelanski, 1955).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.38% in a commercial product, human skin
evidence.support_text: Tribehenin, at 0.38% in a commercial product, was negative in a repeated-insult patch test on human skin, indicating no evidence of skin sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1.68% in a commercial product, human skin
evidence.support_text: Tristearin, at 1.68% in a commercial product, was negative in a repeated-insult patch test on human skin, indicating no evidence of skin sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 40% in a commercial product, human skin
evidence.support_text: Trilaurin, at 40% in a commercial product, was negative in a repeated-insult patch test on human skin, indicating no evidence of skin sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 5% Phytantriol, repeated-insult patch test, 206 human volunteers
evidence.support_text: Phytantriol had no adverse effects in any of the 206 volunteer subjects who underwent a repeated-insult patch test at a 5% concentration.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 4% (4720 µg/cm²), 101 volunteers
evidence.support_text: When 4% (4720 µg/cm²) benzyl cinnamate was tested in a standard repeated insult patch test in 101 volunteers, it also did not produce sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse; DC from mice treated with UVA prior to TCSA; DC co-cultured with lymphocytes from TCSA-photosensitized mice. Also LC treated with UVA prior to TCSA.
evidence.support_text: DC prepared from mice treated with UVA prior to TCSA were nonstimulatory. Untreated LC, and LC treated with UVA prior to TCSA, were without effect.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human DNCB-specific T cell clones co-cultured with autologous EBV-transformed B cells as APCs; response measured by proliferation or cytokine production
evidence.support_text: The human immune response to DNCB is mediated by both CD4+ and CD8+ Th1/Tc1 T cell subtypes. Using DNCB-specific T cell clones and autologous EBV-B cells as APCs, hapten presentation occurs via both metabolism-dependent and -independent pathways: responses of some clones were abrogated by glutaraldehyde fixation of APCs, while others responded to fixed APCs pulsed with DNCB.

evidence.assay_type: T-cell activation assay (comparative to contact sensitizers)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Human T cells; autologous DCs loaded with phenol-exposed melanoma or HaCat cells.
evidence.support_text: TBP induced T-cell responses that recognized both phenol-exposed melanoma cells and phenol-(un)exposed Hacat cells, corresponding to the mode of action of contact sensitizers, thus classifying TBP as a contact sensitizer in this assay system.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human T cells cultured with autologous dendritic cells loaded with phenol-exposed (IC25 and IC12.5) melanoma cells; 1 week culture; activation measured by TNFα, IFNγ, CD137.
evidence.support_text: TBP induced T-cell responses that recognized both phenol-exposed melanoma and HaCat cells, corresponding to the mode of action of contact sensitizers. Table 2 lists CD8 T-cell activation for TBP as '2' (much stronger than BOP), confirming positive CD8 T-cell activation.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human T cells cultured with autologous dendritic cells loaded with phenol-exposed melanoma cells; 1 week.
evidence.support_text: BOP is the reference for CD8 T-cell activation in Table 2, with value 'ref', indicating positive induction of CD8 T-cell responses.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human T cells cultured with autologous dendritic cells loaded with phenol-exposed melanoma cells; 1 week.
evidence.support_text: MOP shows CD8 T-cell activation with value '0' (comparable to BOP) in Table 2.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human T cells cultured with autologous dendritic cells loaded with phenol-exposed melanoma cells; 1 week.
evidence.support_text: POP shows CD8 T-cell activation with value '1' (stronger than BOP) in Table 2.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human T cells cultured with autologous dendritic cells loaded with phenol-exposed melanoma cells; 1 week; activation measured by TNFα, IFNγ, CD137.
evidence.support_text: All phenols tested, except TBP and hydroquinone, induced quinone binding and pigment cell-specific T-cell responses, indicating hydroquinone is negative for pigment cell-specific T-cell activation.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human buffy coat CD4+ T cells; stimulation with TNBS-modified APCs; 5 h incubation
evidence.support_text: Incubation with TNBS-modified APC increased frequencies of CD154+CD4+ T cells to 0.08% ± 0.04% in naive cells after 5 h, compared to control-stimulated background of 0.04% ± 0.05% (n = 11 buffy coats).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human buffy coat CD4+ T cells; stimulation with TNBS-modified APCs; 5 h incubation
evidence.support_text: Incubation with TNBS-modified APC increased frequencies of CD154+CD4+ T cells to 0.09% ± 0.07% in memory cells after 5 h, compared to control-stimulated background of 0.05% ± 0.05% (n = 11 buffy coats).

evidence.experimental_conditions: patch tested on upper back; dipivefrine chlorhydrate 1% aq; readings at day 2 and day 4
evidence.support_text: The patient was patch tested to individual components of Diopine®; there was a strong reaction to dipivefrine chlorhydrate 1% aq at D2 (++) and D4 (+++).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch tested with dipivefrine chlorhydrate 1% aqueous; readings at D2 and D4.
evidence.support_text: There was a strong reaction to dipivefrine chlorhydrate 1% aq at D2 (++) and D4 (+++).

evidence.support_text: One of 18 control tests with sodium amidotrizoate gave a weak positive. He had undergone renography several years earlier.

evidence.support_text: In the initial patch test (Table 1), Case 1 showed a negative reaction to sodium amidotrizoate 25% aq. (24 h: -, 48 h: NT, 72 h: -).

evidence.support_text: In the retest (Table 2), Case 2 showed a positive reaction to sodium amidotrizoate 25% aq. with + at 72 h.

review_policy.eligible_subject: unique measurement-producing subject, donor, or cell-system species
